Inhaler steroids may affect how patients with asthma perceive dyspnea (shortness of breath) during periods of bronchospasm (narrowing of the airways). Research has shown that elevated eosinophil counts in the airway wall can increase pulmonary dysfunction and perception of dyspnea. Inhaled corticosteroids, which are typically used to reduce inflammation in asthma, may decrease PD (perceived dyspnea) by reducing eosinophilic inflammation. This suggests that steroids could help alleviate symptoms associated with bronchoconstriction.

It's essential to note that the current evidence is not conclusive, and more research is needed to fully understand the relationship between inhaled corticosteroids and dyspnea perception during bronchospasm. However, based on the available data, it appears that steroids may be beneficial in reducing PD symptoms in patients with asthma.

Keep in mind that individuals with asthma should consult their healthcare provider for personalized advice on managing symptoms and improving control of their condition.
